condition: where banks keep their head offices
state: eight banks decided to move their head offices from Sana'a to Aden
note: Banks named at line 21: Tadhamon Bank, Al-Kuraimi Islamic Microfinance Bank, Shamil Bank of Yemen and Bahrain, Yemeni Islamic Bank, Saba Islamic Bank, Yemen Gulf Bank, Yemeni Commercial Bank, Al-Amal Microfinance Bank.

condition: whether electronic funds transfer is an accepted means of payment
state: accepted (وسيلة مقبولة لإجراء الدفع)
note: Law No. 40 of 2006 on payment systems and electronic financial and banking operations, Art. 26; Art. 46 makes it effective from issue, dated 28 December 2006 (lines 237-241).

condition: legal effect of electronic contracts, records and signatures
state: same legal effect as written documents and signatures
note: Law No. 40 of 2006, Art. 10.

condition: whether offer and acceptance may be made by electronic message
state: an information message is a legally accepted way to make an offer or acceptance
note: Law No. 40 of 2006, Art. 15(a).

condition: who may operate ATMs
state: licensed banks, in numbers the Central Bank sets, and financial institutions the Central Bank licenses under its conditions
note: Law No. 40 of 2006, Art. 8(1), among the powers of the Bank (the Central Bank of Yemen, defined at line 52).

condition: duties of institutions providing electronic funds transfer
state: comply with the Central Bank and banks laws and the rules issued under them; take measures to provide safe services to customers and keep banking secrecy
note: Law No. 40 of 2006, Art. 27 (lines 176-178).

condition: payer's liability for unauthorized electronic debits
state: not liable for unauthorized debits made after notifying the bank or institution; liable where his own negligence mainly contributed and the bank did its duties
note: Law No. 40 of 2006, Arts. 28 and 29.

condition: who approves electronic payment means
state: the Central Bank, by instructions it issues
note: Law No. 40 of 2006, Art. 30; Art. 7(2)(a) (line 102) gives the Bank regulatory and supervisory powers over electronic operations.

condition: who may issue electronic-signature certificates or provide electronic-signature services
state: only entities licensed under the executive regulation
note: Law No. 40 of 2006, Art. 43.

condition: general sales tax rate on goods and services sold
state: 5% of the value of sales of goods and services, domestic and imported, outside the exempt, zero-rated and specific-rate items
note: Law No. 42 of 2005 amending Law No. 19 of 2001 on the General Sales Tax, Art. 4(a); Art. 4(b) (line 82) sets 5% of consumer price on petrol, diesel, kerosene, fuel oil and butane. Effective from issue, dated 18 July 2005 (lines 524-532).

condition: annual sales above which a seller must register for sales tax
state: a threshold the Minister sets by regulation, not less than YER 50,000,000 of taxable sales a year
note: Law No. 42 of 2005, Art. 6(a)(1)-(2): at the threshold a person must register with the Tax Authority as a taxpayer (line 98).

condition: how often a registered seller must file a sales tax return
state: for every tax period, within 21 days after the end of the previous month, whether or not tax is due
note: Law No. 42 of 2005, Art. 13.

condition: services exempt from sales tax
state: financial and banking services; insurance; health; education; non-profit NGO services; some domestic land transport; residential letting; water, sewerage and electricity; cleaning; restoration of monuments; pilgrimage agencies; hotels of one star or less
note: Law No. 42 of 2005, Schedule 1 (lines 248-370).

condition: goods exempt from sales tax
state: wheat and wheat flour; rice; medicines; raw gold; travellers' personal effects; circulating notes and coins
note: Law No. 42 of 2005, Art. 40(b), list at lines 192-202.

condition: sales tax rate on exported goods and services
note: Law No. 42 of 2005, Schedule 2 (lines 376-411), which also zero-rates international transport and port services and infant milk.

condition: sales tax rates on specific goods and services
state: rates set item by item in Schedule 3
note: Law No. 42 of 2005, Schedule 3 (lines 415-522) lists: cigarettes 90% of consumer price; cigars 90%; qat 20% of consumer price; arms and ammunition 90%; gold 2% and 3%; mobile phone services 10%; international phone services 10%.

condition: when sales tax on imported goods is paid
state: before release from customs, except production inputs and capital goods of registered manufacturers who keep regular records
note: Law No. 42 of 2005, Art. 34(a).

condition: how sales tax on qat is collected
state: tax officials collect it in qat markets, at city entrances or places the Tax Authority sets, outside registration, returns and invoices; collection by farming-out (القبالة) or contracting is banned
note: Law No. 42 of 2005, Art. 64 (line 236).

condition: how much cash a bank customer can withdraw
state: banks give each customer withdrawing from a balance or exchanging foreign currency only YER 80,000 a day
place: areas controlled by the legitimate government
note: The article (line 31) places the liquidity crisis in the areas under the legitimate government's control.

condition: rial price of one US dollar
place: areas controlled by the legitimate government
note: Given in parentheses in the article on the liquidity crisis in the legitimate government's areas (line 31).

condition: which banknotes merchants accept
state: merchants refuse torn and damaged notes, which are over 70% of notes in circulation
place: areas controlled by the legitimate government
note: Stated by a source close to the Central Bank in Aden; place from line 31.

condition: whether buyers have digital transfers available
state: not available to the great majority of the rural population

condition: whether exchange companies may open accounts and take deposits
state: not permitted, though several exchange companies did so
note: The article (lines 30-34) is about exchange companies in the Houthi-controlled areas.

condition: whether depositors can draw their bank deposits
state: commercial banks stopped paying out depositors' money since 2016
note: Since 2016, after the Houthis took over the banking sector (same line).

condition: where merchants and households keep their savings
state: with exchange companies, as a substitute for the disabled banks
note: Shop owners, expatriates, sellers and daily workers.

condition: whether customers of a failed exchange company are compensated from its licence guarantee
state: a guarantee is required at licensing for that purpose, but compensation is not applied in practice

condition: which money transfer networks may operate
state: the central bank branch in Sana'a stopped dealing with major exchange firms and transfer networks

condition: how money transfers can be made
state: restricted, tied to one specified network, with strict ceilings
note: Follows the Houthi decision to separate the banking system in their areas from the Central Bank in Aden; over 14 exchange firms closed in Sana'a in the three months before the article.

condition: whether exchange companies may use the unified network of the Central Bank in Aden
state: banned (منع التعامل مع الشبكة الموحدة)
note: Per the exchangers' association in Sana'a; transfers with government-controlled areas also restricted.

condition: what an exchange company closed by the central bank must do to resume
state: often only after paying sums through 'back doors' (بوابات خلفية)
note: Workers in the exchange sector, about the central bank branch's management (line 64).

condition: who may pay out remittances from abroad
state: only banks and exchange companies qualified and approved by the Central Bank in Aden
note: The source says the decision binds all bank and exchange branches in the Houthi-controlled areas, which cannot do this without prior licence (YE-D033).

condition: through whom licensed providers may pay out remittances from abroad
state: their head offices authorised from Aden and their branches, plus sub-agencies on annual contracts with local exchange firms
note: Decision signed by the Governor of the Central Bank, Ahmed Ghaleb Al-Maabqi; place as in YE-D033.

condition: currency in which remittances from abroad are paid out
state: in the currency received, without conversion, or as the beneficiary decides
note: Central Bank in Aden decision; place as in YE-D033.

condition: currency in which remittances from abroad are paid out
state: not in US dollars: the Houthis banned paying out remittances in dollars
note: The source says the Houthis do this now (الآن).

condition: where banks keep their head offices
state: the Central Bank in Aden gave all commercial banks a deadline, ending two days after the article, to move their head offices from Sana'a to Aden

condition: whether buyers can pay with a mobile e-wallet
state: available: Aden Cash wallet of Aden Islamic Bank for Microfinance, under licence of the Central Bank of Yemen, for financial transactions by mobile phone
note: The bank's own service page; the bank's address is in Aden (line 40).

condition: which rial banknotes may be used
state: new notes printed by the Aden central bank banned; residents had 30 days to swap them for old notes or electronic rials
note: Ban by the Houthi-controlled central bank in Sana'a, mid-December 2019.
